spec.user_stories: - As the journal owner, I want a Next button on the logs list that shows the next older logs, so I can read entries older than the newest 5. - As the journal owner, I want a Previous button that returns to newer logs, so I can move back. - As the journal owner, I want every page, and the order inside it, to be newest to oldest, with page 1 holding the newest logs. - As an API client, I want an optional offset on GET /api/logs, so I can fetch older logs with the same limit and ordering. - As an existing client, I want the response shape and the no-parameter behavior unchanged (bare list, newest 5).
spec.acceptance_criteria: Backend 1. GET /api/logs?offset=K (integer K >= 0) skips the K newest logs in the order created_at DESC, id DESC and returns the following logs, up to limit (default 5, max 20 as in T023). Status 200. 2. With 12 logs stored, limit=5 at offset=0, 5 and 10 returns 5, 5 and 2 logs. The three pages share no id, and concatenated they equal the full newest-first order (all 12 ids, each exactly once). This holds when created_at is out of id order and when several logs share one created_at (higher id first). 3. An offset equal to or greater than the number of stored logs returns 200 and []. This includes 0 logs stored, and a large offset such as 1000000. 4. offset=0 and an absent offset behave identically, and a request with no query parameters returns exactly what T023 returned (newest 5). 5. A negative offset (-1) or a non-integer offset ("abc", "", "2.5") returns 422 with the API's usual error JSON and no logs. An offset too large for the database (e.g. 99999999999999999999) returns 422 or [], never 500. 6. limit rules are unchanged: limit below 1 or non-integer gives 422, above 20 is clamped to 20, and clamping applies together with offset (offset=5&limit=100 returns logs 6 to 25 of the order). 7. Each returned log carries exactly its own photos (position then id order) on every page. Photos are read only for the ids on the returned page. 8. Response format is unchanged: a bare JSON list of objects with exactly id, description, photos, created_at, updated_at. No envelope, total count or new header. 9. POST, PUT and DELETE behavior and the 500 handling of GET /api/logs are unchanged. 10. New backend tests cover criteria 1 to 7 and use only TEST_DATABASE_URL and the temporary uploads folder. The full existing suite passes. Frontend (checkable by driving the page in a browser with more than 10 logs stored in the test database; page size is 5) 11. On load the list shows the newest 5 logs, newest first. A Previous button and a Next button are present in the logs area as real button elements with visible text, reachable by keyboard. 12. With 12 logs: page 1 shows logs 1-5 (newest), Next shows 6-10, Next again shows 11-12, then Next is disabled. Previous goes back one page each time and shows the same logs as before. Previous is disabled on page 1. Within every page the order is newest to oldest, and no log appears on two pages. 13. Next is enabled only if an older log exists beyond the current page, and this is decided without changing the API response format (the page requests one more log than it shows and does not render the extra one). With exactly 5 logs, Next is disabled; with exactly 6, Next is enabled on page 1 and page 2 shows 1 log. 14. When all logs fit on one page (0 to 5 logs), both buttons are hidden or both are disabled (the implementer picks one and uses it consistently). With 0 logs the existing empty message still shows. 15. While a page is loading, both buttons are disabled; they are re-enabled by state afterward (disabled only per criteria 12 and 13). Rapid double clicks on Next advance one page per completed load, never skipping a page. 16. Creating a log successfully returns the view to page 1, where the new log is first. Editing a log successfully keeps the current page and the same logs on it. Deleting a log reloads the current page; if that page is now empty and it is not page 1, the view steps back one page (e.g. deleting the only log on page 3 shows page 2). Deleting while on page 1 stays on page 1. 17. Paging while an edit form is open closes the form (edit state resets, the normal view of the logs is shown) and discards the unsaved edit; no stale form remains on the new page. 18. A failed page load (e.g. server down or HTTP error) shows the existing load-error message in the same way as today, and the buttons end in a safe state: the user can retry by clicking the same button or reloading; a failed load must not change the displayed page number to one that is not shown. 19. The buttons follow the page's light and dark theme tokens (legible text and visible disabled state in both themes), use the existing button style conventions, and expose state through the disabled attribute. The group has an accessible name (for example a labelled nav or group) and the buttons are not announced as enabled when disabled. 20. Reloading the browser page returns to page 1 (no persisted page number is required). Docs 21. specs.md documents offset (default 0, >= 0, 422 on invalid values), the unchanged ordering and bare-list response, and replaces T023's note that older logs are unreachable in the UI with the paging behavior. README.md is updated only if it describes endpoint or UI behavior.
spec.assumptions: - Orchestrator design guidance adopted without deviation: offset is an optional integer >= 0, 422 below 0 or non-integer; page size 5; response stays a bare list; the frontend requests limit=6 and renders 5. - No page number display, jump-to-page or total count is required (the API has no total). A "Page N" label is optional. - Hidden versus both-disabled buttons for a single page is the implementer's choice (criterion 14). - Page position lives in JavaScript memory only; reload returns to page 1. - A very large offset is handled as 422 or [] (either is acceptable; never 500). - The frontend page size is a constant of 5 matching the T023 default; the frontend does not rely on the server default. - Concurrent changes by another client between page loads can cause a log to repeat or be skipped across pages; this is accepted for offset paging in a single-user app.
spec.edge_cases: - 0, 5, 6, 10, 11 logs stored: button states and page contents. - Exactly 10 logs: page 2 is the last page and Next is disabled there. - Deleting the last log of the last page (not page 1) steps back; deleting the only log while on page 1 shows the empty message. - Deleting the last log of page 2 when page 3 exists does not step back (page 2 refills from older logs). - Creating a log while on page 3 returns to page 1. - Editing a log on page 2 leaves the user on page 2. - Logs with identical created_at across a page boundary: no duplicate and no gap (id DESC tie-break). - Delete or save failing (error shown) leaves the page and buttons unchanged. - Edit form open, then Next or Previous clicked. - Delete confirm dialog cancelled: nothing changes. - Theme toggled while a button is disabled.

risks.risk: The limit=6 look-ahead means the frontend depends on the server not clamping below 6; the maximum is 20 so it is safe, but a future change to the maximum or default must be checked against the frontend.
Offset paging can repeat or skip logs if data changes between loads (other tab, delete). Accepted for a single-user app; mention in specs.md notes.

Stale responses: a slow earlier load finishing after a later one could overwrite the view. The implementation must keep the shown page and buttons consistent with the last requested page (criteria 15 and 18).
Existing loadLogs is called by save, edit and delete flows; changing its signature or state handling can break their post-action reload behavior (criterion 16).

No frontend unit tests exist and none may be added; frontend criteria are verified only by driving the page, so the verifier needs a seeded test database and a free high port (not 8000, not the real dailylog database or uploads/).

spec.dependencies: - backend/database.py (list_logs), backend/routes.py (list_logs endpoint and _list), backend/models.py (limits and constants), frontend/app.js, frontend/index.html, frontend/style.css, specs.md, backend/tests/. - T023 behavior (limit default 5, max 20, ordering) as the baseline. - No new packages and no JS test framework. A PostgreSQL database ending in _test through TEST_DATABASE_URL for tests.
spec.self_critique: Stories map to criteria: Next/Previous and fetching old logs (11-13, 1-3), ordering (2, 12), API offset (1-6), unchanged format (4, 8, 9), post-action behavior (16, 17). Criteria are observable through HTTP responses or the DOM. The biggest risk is the frontend state handling around concurrent loads and the post-delete step-back, which is specified but easy to get subtly wrong. A smaller uncertainty is that the 422-versus-[] choice for an overflow offset is left open on purpose.
